Happy Wednesday! It's **Swin** and **Martin**. As we prepare for Thanksgiving,
one thing to be thankful for is how unyieldingly dumb the sitting president of
the United States is. The vastness of his stupidity has its many drawbacks,
but it can also lead to profound clarity and an abundance of self-
incrimination.

In today's '**First Draft, '** we'll get into **Donald Trump 's** seemingly
chronic inability to make the ballooning scandal engulfing his administration
about anything other than _me, me, me, me, me_. Plus, **Kilmar Ábrego Garcia**
leaves the U.S. voluntarily for Spain, ending the Trump administration's
vicious pursuit, and there's a lot more news to consider. Let's dive in.

## **China, China, China**

Earlier this month, as the Nvidia scandal began exploding to such an extent
that the Trump-Vance administration couldn't just brush it aside as they do to
every atrocity they commit, some of Donald Trump's most brain-drained
defenders - including his "science and technology" adviser, David Sacks -
started insisting that this scandal _must be Russiagate 2.0_ , some anti-Trump
or Deep State-spawned HOAX, to be dismissed out of hand.

We are not going to waste time relitigating the Trump-Russia saga from Trump's
first presidency (though do yourself a favor and read **Prem 's** piece
**"[Russiagate Was Real, Trump Admits,](https://zeteo.com/p/trump-russia-
interference-real)"** from July). But even if you agree with the spin that so-
called Russiagate was "fake" all along, it's getting embarrassingly hard, more
so each day, to claim Trump's brand new Chinagate scandal is anything but very
real.

This time, there is no Deep State to blame. There's no James Comey analog. If
this is, in the mind of Trumpists, RUSSIAGATE THE SECOND COMING, then that
would mean this president and some of his highest-ranking political appointees
and loyalists are doing Russiagate to themselves, for fun, on purpose.

[Subscribe now](https://zeteo.com/subscribe)

One reason for this is that Trump keeps talking to reporters to confirm not
only key details of the massive scandal but also his own involvement.

And some of the president's advisers are pissed. Here's what we're hearing:

For starters, Trump has [stated](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/trump-letting-
nvidia-sell-h200-advanced-chips-china/), plainly, that he himself relaxed U.S.
rules on what Nvidia AI chips could be sold to China. U.S. officials have
consistently argued that there are certain AI chips that, as a matter of
national security, need to be kept out of the Chinese government's grasp. But
this administration only pretends to be full of China hawks, and in fact will
instantly bend over backward to coddle Trump's personal "friend," President Xi
Jinping.

Consider the Nvidia scandal so far. As reported by the _New York Times_ ,
Secretary of State Marco Rubio [warned top
officials](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/08/us/politics/rubio-nvidia-ceo-
chinese-spy.html) last spring that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was in a
relationship with a suspected Chinese spy. Huang was left off the guest list
for Trump's trip to China in May. Trump made sure he was included. The _Times_
also revealed that Trump knew about Huang's affair, and chose not to take
action. Earlier this month, asked if he regretted that decision, Trump told
reporters:** "No, I don't think so. I think [Huang is] an honorable guy. I
think he probably has an excuse for it. You have to hear it."**

The _Times_ also
[reported](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/12/us/politics/lutnick-nvidia-
commerce-china-chips.html) that Trump's longtime friend turned commerce
secretary, Howard Lutnick, continually took a softer line on the matter of
Nvidia selling AI chips to Chinese companies including Megaspeed, the company
that employed the suspected spy who loved Huang, even as others in the
administration advocated a crackdown. And as the _Times_ put it, **" Mr.
Lutnick's defenders have repeatedly argued that when it came to Nvidia, he was
doing what the president wanted."**

As **Zeteo** reported this week, after Huang was forced out of his company,
Trump **"[made it a priority](https://zeteo.com/p/trump-nvidia-jensen-huang-
job-back)"** to get his friend his job back, personally working the phones to
bully Nvidia to rehire him, directing senior officials to do the same, and
marshaling considerable government resources towards corruptly resurrecting
the professional fortunes of his outside adviser and buddy.

It is no exaggeration to say that the president of the United States made this
the first order of business, at a time when his fellow citizens continue to
suffer under the weight of his fascist bumbling and malaise-filled economy.

Furthermore, one funny (albeit darkly) thing that Trump advisers both in and
out of the White House have vented to us recently is their anger or
frustration at President Trump for making it harder to simply find a
convenient scapegoat and begin to move on. According to sources with direct
knowledge of the situation, since the dawn of this Nvidia news cycle, several
senior officials have yearned to shovel all the blame for this colossal mess
onto Lutnick, in the hopes of convincing Trump to fire him and try to skate
past the matter.

The problem? Trump, the sources say, keeps standing by his friend Lutnick (who
is _widely_ despised, even within this shambolic administration), and also
won't stop vociferously and publicly taking ownership of the scandal, while
deepening and extending it!

On Monday, when Huang was reinstated at Nvidia, Trump bragged it was all his
doing. **" I convinced them,"** [he told
CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/23/trump-nvidia-jensen-huang.html). **" I
made the deal."**

[Share](https://zeteo.com/p/trumps-advisers-want-a-
scapegoat?utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&action=share)

**" The president is relentless at wrapping this scandal around himself,"**
one Trump adviser tells us, sharing the broader annoyance at the fact that the
president is still backing Lutnick and making the story all about Trump,
Trump, Trump - all while insisting the whole administration carries the
baggage with him. (Some officials, such as Rubio, have presidential ambitions
and do not want to be tied to this. And yet!) Moreover, a Trump official
involved with this fiasco tells us that they believe the president is publicly
giving the incoming Democratic congressional majority more and more ammunition
for expected investigations and subpoenas into the Nvidia affair: **" Please
stop [talking],"** this source says, describing their incredibly private
version of what they'd like to tell the president to do.

Basically: All of Trump's public and private actions on this matter amount to
him, and his inner circle, taking the fullest of ownership of this very real
Chinagate scandal. On Tuesday, for example, Trump lawyer-turned-Attorney
General Todd Blanche got dutifully, performatively mad. Asked if Huang had
been investigated, Blanche [huffed](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/trump-
administration/todd-blanche-nvidia-investigation-ceo-jensen-huang-trump-
rcna611132):** "What does that mean, had Huang been investigated? For what? I
don't understand the question… It's certainly not fair to him to just
speculate about, about things or answer hypothetical questions. And so, so
no."**

Such behavior is infuriating to the very people who can't just come out and
blame and trash the president by name. Still, some prominent Trump advisers
and close allies _are_ now airing their displeasure in public, if of course
without going straight at the God Emperor himself. Former House Speaker Newt
Gingrich, who still counsels Trump in an outside capacity, posted online:

Yeah. We gotta find out who in the **" federal bureaucracy"** is behind
this!!!

## **🇮 🇷 Iran War Updates**

  * **Decapitation option:** The Trump administration is considering whether to illegally assassinate 'hardline' senior Iranian leaders as a way to bring the war to an end, NBC [reported](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/national-security/trump-administration-officials-debating-targeting-irans-leaders-source-rcna610889).

  * **Iran demands:** Iranian Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf [said](https://apnews.com/article/mideast-iran-gaza-israel-houthis-libya-november-24-2026-ba01cb036a849ba69873da5000ee08d5) Tehran would not negotiate further until seven unnamed conditions are met. Previous demands have included lifting sanctions, unfreezing assets, and ending the U.S. naval blockade. Iran also said three oil tankers were on fire after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz.

  * **Dems warned:** University of Maryland polling [showed](https://x.com/ShibleyTelhami/status/2125236208603467995/photo/1) 80% of Democrats and 55% of all voters want the Iran War over regardless of terms.****[Demand Progress](https://www.demandprogress.org/)/YouGov showed 76% of voters who backed Kamala Harris in 2024 would be less likely to vote for a candidate who backs war spending in a must-pass government funding bill.

  * **Houthis advance:** Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen [advanced](https://apnews.com/article/mideast-iran-gaza-israel-houthis-libya-november-24-2026-ba01cb036a849ba69873da5000ee08d5) close to the port of Aden, the government based there said, adding that it was digging in to defend the city while an evacuation order was issued for Hodeidah. The Saudi-backed government blamed the Houthis for shelling that killed three people, including a child. In Saudi Arabia, 11 were injured by a strike on a tower in Riyadh.

  * **Lebanon latest:** Aid group Doctors Without Borders [said](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/latest/civilians-and-health-care-remain-under-attack-lebanon) a new report "captures how Israeli strikes have killed or maimed children, the elderly, and entire families" in southern Lebanon. "Medical facilities and ambulances were directly struck or affected by Israeli attacks at a time of heightened medical and humanitarian needs, while under pressure from repeated influxes of mass casualties," it added.

Ábrego Garcia arrives with his wife Jennifer Vasquez Sura at court in
Greenbelt, Maryland, on Dec. 22, 2025. Photo: Alex Wong/Getty Images._

Kilmar Ábrego Garcia, the Salvadoran immigrant unlawfully deported to an El
Salvador mega prison last year, left the U.S. on Tuesday night "a free man -
unharmed and with dignity," Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen
[said](https://x.com/ChrisVanHollen/status/2125386746917466415/photo/1).

Ábrego Garcia came to the U.S. at age 18, claiming to have been threatened by
gangs in El Salvador - a threat accepted by an immigration judge who let him
stay. Ábrego Garcia married a U.S. citizen and had children but still found
himself caught up in mass deportations at the start of Trump's second
presidency, and sent to El Salvador's infamous torture prison CECOT.

As the case attracted publicity - the Trump administration traducing Ábrego
Garcia as a criminal and gang member and ignoring court orders for his return
- Van Hollen flew to El Salvador to see him.

After three months, a U.S. Supreme Court decision finally saw Ábrego Garcia
returned to American soil, only for the Trump administration to press criminal
charges. Ábrego Garcia beat the Trump administration again, with a judge
dismissing that case and finding it to have been a vindictive prosecution. The
administration _continued_ to try to deport their target, this time to African
countries.

On Tuesday, the _Washington Post_
[reported](https://www.washingtonpost.com/immigration/2026/11/24/kilmar-
abrego-garcia/) that Ábrego Garcia had negotiated a deal to leave voluntarily
and was headed to Spain.

"Today, Kilmar is traveling to a country of his choice, a free man, unharmed
and with dignity," Van Hollen said in a
[statement](https://x.com/ChrisVanHollen/status/2125386746917466415/photo/1).

"While the Trump administration had been pursuing their vindictive prosecution
against Kilmar and desperately trying to ship him against his will to
countries known for human rights abuses, the administration was forced to come
to this agreement that respects Kilmar's will and the due process rights
guaranteed to him and to all in our nation.

"I am relieved that he will be safe, in a country of his choosing, and free -
including from this administration's constant persecution."

An attorney for Ábrego Garcia, Sean Hecker, said: "We will always admire his
remarkable courage in staring down and defeating a vindictive prosecution
instigated by the highest reaches of the Justice Department. He, in turn, is
grateful to those who stood by him."

## **🌏 Anywhere But America**

  * **🇵 🇸 Don't forget Gaza: **At least nine people, including a child and three police officers, were [killed](https://apnews.com/article/mideast-iran-gaza-israel-houthis-libya-november-24-2026-ba01cb036a849ba69873da5000ee08d5) in Israeli strikes overnight Monday and on Tuesday morning, officials said, adding that Na'im Abu Nahl, director-general of the Interior Ministry, was among the dead. 

  * **🇵 🇸 Human shields: **_Haaretz_ [reported](https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/israel-security/2026-11-24/ty-article/.premium/israeli-military-probing-use-of-palestinians-as-human-shields-in-the-west-bank/000001a2-0a3b-d0d9-a9f6-befbaddd0000) the practice of using civilians as human shields, officially banned by the Israeli military but used in Gaza, is also being still being used by Israeli soldiers in the occupied West Bank.

  * 🇷🇺🇺🇦 **Costs of war:** A Russian glide bomb attack on Zaporizhzhia in southern Ukraine [killed](https://apnews.com/article/russia-ukraine-libya-sea-drone-attacks-bfff959fb4c7415f9473b34e78a4f750) two civilians and wounded 48. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he was sending reinforcements to the region, while outlining a need for an extra $27.4 billion in aid from other countries next year.

  * **🇿 🇼 War lure: **A Zimbabwean man was [convicted](https://apnews.com/article/south-africa-zimbabwe-russia-recruits-war-33c3fc1606d01947b713616424a79c4f) in South Africa for trying to travel to Russia to fight in the war against Ukraine for pay. Four others are negotiating plea deals.

  * **🇨 🇳 Guilty verdict:** Chinese telecoms giant Huawei was [convicted](https://www.reuters.com/legal/litigation/chinas-huawei-convicted-us-criminal-trial-stemming-iran-business-2026-11-24/) by a jury in New York City on criminal charges of deceiving banks about business in Iran and stealing U.S. trade secrets.
